content: Heliox is a specialized breathing gas composed of a mixture of helium (He) and oxygen (O2). Its use in medical settings dates back to the 1930s. Initially, it was employed to alleviate symptoms associated with upper airway obstruction. Over time, its applications have expanded significantly, primarily due to the gas's low density. Beyond medical uses, Heliox is also utilized in saturation diving and occasionally during the deep phases of technical diving. In medical practice, Heliox typically refers to a mixture containing 21% oxygen (the same concentration as in ambient air) and 79% helium, although other ratios are available depending on clinical needs. The resistance to airflow in the airways is influenced by both the diameter of the airways and the density of the gas being inhaled. By replacing nitrogen, a major component of air, with helium, the density of the inhaled gas is reduced. This reduction in density leads to a decrease in airway resistance. Consequently, breathing Heliox requires less mechanical effort to ventilate the lungs, thereby reducing the Work of Breathing (WOB). Heliox is primarily used to manage medical conditions that involve a narrowing of the airways, which increases airway resistance. Such conditions include upper airway obstruction, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), bronchiolitis, and croup. Patients suffering from these conditions often experience symptoms such as dyspnea (difficulty breathing), hypoxemia (low oxygen levels in the blood), and fatigue of the respiratory muscles due to overexertion. If untreated, these symptoms can progress to respiratory failure, necessitating intubation and mechanical ventilation. Heliox can mitigate these effects by reducing airway resistance and the associated work of breathing, thereby making it easier for patients to breathe and potentially preventing respiratory failure. Additionally, Heliox has proven useful in facilitating the weaning process for patients transitioning off mechanical ventilation. It is also employed to enhance the delivery of inhalable medications during nebulization therapy.
